# SEO-164: Use absolute canonical URLs inside structured data

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| --- | --- |

| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

Every url, @id, contentUrl, thumbnailUrl, and image value in the markup is an absolute URL on the production origin, and page-level url values match the page's canonical.

## Rationale

A relative or origin-inconsistent value cannot be resolved reliably outside the page it appeared in, so the node it identifies cannot be matched against the same node referenced from another page.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_structured_data"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Resolve every URL-valued property through the same builder that produces canonical values, so the origin comes from configuration once. Do not emit a path-only value on the assumption the consumer will resolve it against the document address.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Collect all URL-valued properties from the parsed markup and report any that lack a scheme and host or whose host differs from the production origin.
- Evidence: `JSON_LD`, `RENDERED_HTML`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: `jsonld-absolute-urls`

- Frameworks: `any`
